result.title: Trigger-Invariant Contrastive Unlearning for Backdoor Removal
result.comment: An extended version of the short paper published at CIKM 2026 (https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3799682.3839969)
result.summary: Backdoor attacks pose a severe threat to modern NLP models by embedding hidden triggers that induce malicious behavior at inference time. Recent unlearning methods such as gradient ascent (GA) attempt to remove backdoors by maximizing the loss on poisoned samples; however, these methods can suffer from a critical limitation: they may shift the trigger's influence to other classes rather than eliminating it. In this work, we propose Trigger-Invariant Contrastive Unlearning (TICU), a framework for mitigating textual backdoor behavior by enforcing prediction and representation invariance to trigger insertion. TICU constructs clean and trigger-inserted counterfactual pairs, then fine-tunes the model so that both inputs produce consistent output distributions and aligned hidden representations. To preserve clean-task performance, TICU also retains the supervised classification loss on clean data and constrains parameter drift from the original model. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets, model architectures, and attack settings show that TICU improves triggered accuracy and reduces trigger-induced prediction shifts compared with existing baselines, while maintaining competitive label-flipping performance and limiting clean-task degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TICU：构造干净与含触发词的反事实样本对，通过微调使两者输出分布一致、隐表示对齐，并保留干净数据的监督损失与参数漂移约束，以去除文本后门而不显著损害正常分类性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「对无关扰动保持表示/预测不变」加「限制参数漂移」的训练目标，可能可供核查用于抑制 LVR 中的视觉旁路与捷径特征，使 latent 状态对非必要扰动稳健；但论文属纯文本安全场景，未涉及视觉证据或多步推理状态。
